speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe exactly where your neck pain is and does it radiate down a specific arm?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To narrow down the cause of your weakness and numbness, can you specify exactly which fingers on your hands are affected by the paresthesias, and do you have any difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning shirts or writing?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of fasciculations and absent reflexes alongside weakness suggests lower motor neuron involvement, which is distinct from simple cervical radiculopathy. I need to assess for upper motor neuron signs to differentiate between conditions like ALS and cervical myelopathy, so do you experience any stiffness, spasticity, or difficulty with balance and walking?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, history of a motor vehicle accident 3 years prior. Social history: 7 sexual partners, uses condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To further characterize the weakness and rule out a systemic process like HIV-associated neuropathy or syphilis, have you noticed any muscle atrophy in your forearms or shoulders, and do you have any bowel or bladder dysfunction?

speaker: Patient
text: Oriented to time, place, and person. Vital signs within normal limits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of upper motor neuron signs (implied by the need to rule out myelopathy/ALS) and lower motor neuron signs (fasciculations, absent reflexes, atrophy) strongly points toward ALS. To confirm this and rule out cervical spondylotic myelopathy given your history, I will request an MRI of the cervical spine and EMG/NCS studies.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The MRI findings of a syrinx in the cervical and thoracic spinal cord are diagnostic for syringomyelia, which explains the lower motor neuron signs at the level of the lesion and potential upper motor neuron signs below it. This condition often presents with a capelike distribution of pain and temperature loss, though weakness and fasciculations are also common due to anterior horn cell involvement.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia
